source.title: Tame distillation and desingularization by p-alterations
source.version: The published Annals article (30 pages, pp. 97–126), freely available from the journal, read completely; locators are its page numbers. arXiv:1508.06255v2 ('final version', 24 pages, SHA-256 24f67ac3…) was compared and has the same statements and numbering.
readSections: 2026-09-29: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 97–126, all pages: §§1–4 and references; page images checked at every source issue.

summary: Temkin strengthens Gabber's ℓ′-alteration theorem so that the resolving alteration has degree divisible only by residue characteristics. Any scheme of finite type over a quasi-excellent threefold has a regular char(X)-alteration with snc boundary, and morphisms admit log smooth char(S)-altered desingularization. The new ingredient is tame distillation: after enlarging, an alteration splits as a tame Galois covering over a char(X)-alteration. It rests on the tameness theorem, that p-closed valued fields are tame, which Temkin deduces from Pank's theorem by decompletion in height one and induction on height. It is globalized with Riemann–Zariski spaces and the openness of tame loci. The desingularization then follows Gabber's proof with Sylow subgroups replaced by distillation. Routing: the valued-field ramification theory becomes a new Part II of Tau Ceti Local fields and ramification. Riemann–Zariski spaces, tame distillation and the desingularization theorems join the pending PrimeToDegreeAlterations Part II of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons (Dittmann–Pop, Jannsen). The log structure of a divisor and log regularity are sources for CR.5:log-algebra.

items.name: Valued fields and valuation rings
items.statement: A valued field is a field k with a non-archimedean (Krull) valuation | | : k → {0} ⊔ Γ, written multiplicatively; k° is its valuation ring and k̃ its residue field.

items.name: Primitive element theorem
items.statement: A finite separable field extension L/K is generated by one element: L = K[t]/(f(t)) for a monic irreducible f.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 2.5.2, p. 109

items.name: Valuative criterion of properness
items.statement: A quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism locally of finite type is proper if and only if it satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proofs of Lemma 3.1.3 and §3.1.5, pp. 113–114

items.name: Local structure of étale algebras (Chevalley)
items.statement: If R → S is of finite presentation and étale at a prime Q, then some localization S_f (f ∉ Q) is standard étale over R, i.e. of the form (R[t]/(f(t)))_g with f monic and f′ invertible.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 3.2.10, p. 117 ([Gro67, IV₄, Th. 18.4.6(ii)])
items.note: The paper uses the local form: an essentially étale extension of valuation rings O_y/O_x is a localization of O_x[t]/(f) with f′(a) a unit.

items.name: de Jong's alteration theorem
items.statement: An integral variety X over a field with a closed Z ⊊ X admits an alteration b : X′ → X (proper, dominant, generically finite, X′ integral) with X′ regular and b⁻¹(Z) an snc divisor ([dJ96, Th. 4.1]).
items.note: L5 plans de Jong's Theorems 4.1 and 6.5; the Galois (Th. 7.3) and semistable (Th. 8.2) variants are item dejong-galois-semistable.

items.name: Raynaud–Gruson flattening by blow-up
items.statement: For a finite-type morphism Y → X with X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, flat and of finite presentation over a dense open of X, there is a blow-up X′ → X, centred outside that open, such that the strict transform of Y is flat and of finite presentation over X′ ([RG71, Th. 5.7.9]; [St, tag 081R]).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proofs of Lemma 3.1.6 and Theorem 3.3.6, pp. 115, 120
items.note: L5 lists 'flattening by blowup, strict transforms' among its tasks.

items.name: Normalization in finite extensions
items.statement: For X noetherian, universally Japanese and integral, and K/k(X) finite, the normalization Nor_K(X) is finite over X; for a fine enough modification X₁ → X (e.g. a flattening blow-up), Nor_L(X₁) is a modification of Y = Nor_L(X).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.3, p. 119; proof of Theorem 3.3.6, p. 120
items.note: L5: 'normalization under the applicable excellence hypotheses'.

items.name: Semistable reduction of multipointed curves after a separable alteration
items.statement: For a flat quasi-projective S-curve with smooth generic fibre and étale horizontal boundary over a normal S, there is a separable alteration S̄ → S and a projective modification X̄ → X ×_S S̄ such that (X̄, Z̄_h) is a semistable multipointed S̄-curve (Steps 1–3 of [IT14b, Th. 3.4]; [Tem10]).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Steps 1–3, p. 122
items.note: L5 task 2 plans the curve-fibration construction and stable/semistable reduction of the family.

items.name: Chart criterion for log smoothness between snc pairs
items.statement: For X, Y regular with snc divisors Z, T and f : X → Y with T ×_Y X ⊆ Z, (X, Z) → (Y, T) is log smooth iff near each x there are regular parameters t_i at y defining T and z_j at x defining Z with (1) f*(t_i) = ∏_j z_j^{l_ij}; (2) the kernel and the torsion of the cokernel of l : Z^s → Z^r are finite of order invertible in k(y); (3) X₀ → Y₀ ×_{Spec Z[t]} Spec Z[z] is smooth for small neighbourhoods.
items.note: CR.5:log-algebra plans Kato's chart criteria 'with torsion-order invertibility conditions'; this is its regular-snc specialization.

items.name: The log structure of a divisor
items.statement: For Z ⊂ X closed with complement i : U → X, M_X := O_X ∩ i_*O_U^× defines a log structure (X, Z); it need not be fine (cuspidal curve Spec k[x², x³], Z = {x = 0}), but when X is regular and Z snc it is fs and log regular. A morphism f with T ×_Y X ⊆ Z induces (X, Z) → (Y, T).
items.note: Routed to CR.5:log-algebra as a source, beside the log structures it constructs.

items.name: Log regular log schemes (Kato)
items.statement: An fs log scheme is log regular if at every point the local ring modulo the ideal generated by the non-units of the log structure is regular of the complementary dimension ([Kat94]; [Niz06]); (X, Z) with X regular and Z snc is the basic example.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §1.2.7, p. 100; proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Step 10, p. 123
items.note: Kato's toric singularities are not in CR.5's text, which plans the log algebra they need. Routed to CR.5:log-algebra as a source.

items.name: P-numbers, P-groups, P-extensions and P-closed fields
items.statement: For a set of primes P (complement P′), a P-number has all prime divisors in P, and P(n) is the set of prime divisors of n. A P-group has P-number order; an algebraic extension L/K is a P-extension if [L′ : K] is a P-number for every finite subextension. P-extensions are transitive and closed under subextensions and filtered unions; every K has a maximal P-extension, which is P-closed (no nontrivial P-extensions); a finite extension of a P-closed field need not be P-closed.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II with the field theory it opens with.

items.name: Split towers and separable distillation
items.statement: A tower L/K/k is split if L = l ⊗_k K for some l/k (l linearly disjoint from K with lK = L). An algebraic extension l/k has a separable distillation l/l_i/k (l_i/k purely inseparable, l/l_i separable) iff l = l_s ⊗_k l_i; every finite l/k has a finite extension l′/k with a separable distillation (separable distillation theorem).
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Henselian valued fields
items.statement: A valued field k is henselian if k° is a henselian local ring; equivalently, the valuation of k extends uniquely to every finite extension l/k.
items.note: Mathlib has HenselianLocalRing but not the unique-extension characterization for Krull valuations. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Ramification theory of henselian valued fields
items.statement: For k henselian with residual characteristic exponent p: the maximal unramified extension k^u, with (k^u)° the strict henselization and Gal(k^u/k) = Gal(k̃^s/k̃); l/k is totally ramified iff it is linearly disjoint from k^u iff l̃/k̃ is purely inseparable; every algebraic l/k splits uniquely as l/m/k with m/k unramified and l/m totally ramified, and l/k is tame when l/m is a p′-extension, in which case [l : k] = [l̃ : k̃]·|l^×/k^×|.
items.note: Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2–3 plan this for local fields only, not for Krull valuations of arbitrary rank. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Tame closure and wild inertia
items.statement: A henselian k has a unique maximal tame extension k^t; the wild inertia W_k = Gal(k^s/k^t) is pro-p, the unique Sylow pro-p subgroup of the inertia group I_k = Gal(k^s/k^u); k^t/k^u is Galois with Gal(k^t/k^u) = Hom(|(k^t)^×|/|k^×|, µ_{k^u}), and |(k^t)^×| is the p′-divisible envelope of |k^×|.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Purely wild extensions
items.statement: For k henselian, an algebraic l/k is purely wild if it is linearly disjoint from k^t; equivalently l/k is a totally ramified p-extension; equivalently l̃/k̃ is purely inseparable and |l^×|/|k^×| is a p-group.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Henselization and the basic ramification tower
items.statement: The henselization k^h has ring of integers the henselization of k°; k^u := (k^h)^u, k^t := (k^h)^t give the tower k^s/k^t/k^u/k^h/k, and the subgroup of Gal(k^s/k) fixing k^h is the decomposition group. An algebraic l/k is tame (unramified) if l^h/k^h is; strictly unramified if moreover l̃ = k̃ (k^h/k is the maximal one); henselian if the valuation extends uniquely; totally ramified (purely wild) if linearly disjoint from k^u (k^t).
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2
items.statement: For a valued field k and finite l/k with l₁, …, l_n the non-isomorphic valued extensions of k on l, l ⊗_k k^h = ∏_i l_i^h.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.3, Lemma 2.3.2 and proof, pp. 104–105
items.note: Semilocal integral closure (Bourbaki) and henselization of semilocal rings (EGA IV 18.6.8). Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.4 (Prüfer)
items.statement: If l/k is finite and A ⊆ l is an integrally closed k°-subalgebra, every localization of A is a valuation ring.
items.note: Mathlib has no Prüfer domains. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.8 (unramified versus étale)
items.statement: For a finite extension l/k of valued fields: l/k unramified (strictly unramified) ⟺ l°/k° essentially étale (strictly essentially étale) ⟸ l°/k° étale (strictly étale); all three are equivalent when the height of k is finite.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.3.7, Lemma 2.3.8 and proof, pp. 105–106
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Tame and separably tame fields
items.statement: A valued field k is tame if k^a = k^t (every algebraic extension is tame) and separably tame if k^s = k^t; tame fields are perfect since purely inseparable extensions are purely wild.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.11 (henselian extensions)
items.statement: An algebraic extension l/k is henselian iff l and k^h are linearly disjoint over k, and then l ⊗_k k^h = l^h.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.2 (the six properties)
items.statement: For R one of strictly unramified, unramified, tame, henselian, totally ramified, purely wild: (i) in a tower m/l/k, m/k is R iff m/l and l/k are; (ii) filtered unions of R-extensions are R; (iii) for any set of these properties, every valued field has a (non-canonical) maximal extension with them.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.4 (splitting k^t/k^u/k^h/k)
items.statement: For a maximal henselian unramified k_hu/k and a maximal tame totally ramified k_rt/k: k^h ⊗_k k_hu = k^u and k^u ⊗_k k_rt = k^t.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: §2.4.6 and Remark 2.4.7 (five equivalent splitting statements)
items.statement: For a class V of valued fields closed under algebraic extensions, with k_w a maximal purely wild extension, the following are equivalent: (0) k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a for some k_w; (1) for every k_w; (2) k_w is tame; (3) k ∈ V is tame iff k = k_w; (4) Gal(k^s/k) → Gal(k^t/k) has a section. They are also equivalent to their separable analogues with a maximal separable purely wild k_sw.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.4.6 and Remark 2.4.7, pp. 108
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.9 (Pank)
items.statement: If k is henselian and k_w is a maximal purely wild extension, then k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a.
items.note: Cited input: Kuhlmann–Pank–Roquette prove (4) by a profinite Schur–Zassenhaus argument and pro-p-freeness of Sylow subgroups; Ershov proves (3) by controlling defect. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Krasner's lemma and continuity of roots
items.statement: Over a henselian valued field, a monic polynomial g of the same degree whose root is close enough to a root of a separable monic f generates the same extension ([End72, 16.8]); roots of monic polynomials depend continuously on the coefficients ([Bri06, Th. 2]).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 2.5.2, p. 109
items.note: Mathlib's IsKrasner covers complete normed fields, not henselian Krull-valued fields. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.5.2 (decompletion)
items.statement: If k has height one, every tower L/k^h/k with L/k^h separable splits: there is a henselian extension l/k with L = l^h = l ⊗_k k^h.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.5.1, Lemma 2.5.2 and proof, p. 109
items.note: k is dense in k^h (k̂ is henselian); Krasner for finite L, Zorn in general. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.3
items.statement: For k of height one and algebraic l/k: l/k is a maximal separable purely wild extension iff l/k is henselian and l^h/k^h is a maximal separable purely wild extension.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Theorem 2.5.5 (Pank's theorem in height one)
items.statement: If k is a valued field of height one and k_w/k a maximal purely wild extension, then k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.5.4, Theorem 2.5.5 and proof, p. 110
items.note: Perfect case via k^h and Corollary 2.5.3; general case via the perfection and the equivalence (0) ⟺ (1). Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.6
items.statement: Any p-closed valued field of height one is tame.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Composed valuations and the chain of a finite-height valuation
items.statement: A valuation ring R̃ of k̃ pulls back to a valuation ring R of k composed of (k, k°) and (k̃, R̃); conversely each prime n ⊂ k° exhibits k° as composed of k°_n and k°/n. For k of height d, k_i = (k, k°_i) with k°_i the localization of height i and k̃_i its residue field; the residual characteristic exponents p_i are 1 for i < n and p for i ≥ n (some n).
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.3(i)
items.statement: For l/k algebraic of height d < ∞ and 0 ≤ i ≤ d: l/k is unramified iff both l_i/k_i and l̃_i/k̃_i are unramified.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.2, Lemma 2.6.3(i) and proof, p. 111
items.note: The 'if' direction is [Tem10, Prop. 2.2.2]. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.3(ii)
items.statement: l/k is tame iff l_i/k_i and l̃_i/k̃_i are tame and |l_i^×|/|k_i^×| has no nontrivial p-torsion (p = exp.char(k̃)); the last condition can be omitted when p_i = p.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.2, Lemma 2.6.3(ii) and proof, pp. 111–112
items.note: The last step of the printed proof writes 'p = char(K̃_i) divides [L̃_i : K̃_i]'; when p_i = 1 the field K̃_i has characteristic 0, and the prime that matters is the residue characteristic p of K̃_i's own valuation (sourceIssues E4). The conclusion holds. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.6.4
items.statement: A valued field k of height d < ∞ is tame iff k_i and k̃_i are tame and |k_i^×| is p-divisible; the divisibility condition can be omitted when p_i = p.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Finite transcendence degree gives finite height
items.statement: A valued field of finite transcendence degree over its prime subfield has finite height (Abhyankar's inequality).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Theorem 2.6.6, p. 112
items.note: Used without citation. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Theorem 2.6.6 (tameness theorem)
items.statement: Let k be a valued field of residual characteristic exponent p. If k is p-closed, then k is tame.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.5, Theorem 2.6.6 and proof, p. 112
items.note: Finite height by induction on d with Corollaries 2.5.6 and 2.6.4; in general, descend a finite l/k to a finitely generated k′ ⊆ k, replaced by its algebraic closure in k, which stays p-closed. The proof cites a nonexistent Corollary 2.5.6(ii) (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: de Jong: Galois alterations and altered semistable reduction
items.statement: The alteration of dJ96 Th. 4.1 can be chosen G-Galois (X′/G → X generically radicial, G = Aut_X(X′)) [dJ96, Th. 7.3]; and an integral scheme over an excellent curve admits altered semistable reduction [dJ96, Th. 8.2].
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Gabber's ℓ′-altered desingularization
items.statement: If ℓ is a prime invertible on X, the altered desingularization and altered semistable reduction theorems hold with alterations of degree prime to ℓ ([IT14b, Ths. 2.1 and 2.4]); more generally ℓ′-altered desingularization of finite-type morphisms [IT14b, Th. 3.5], via relative curves [IT14b, Th. 3.4]; in characteristic 0 an actual desingularization of morphisms [IT14b, Th. 3.9].
items.note: The theorem PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and PAPER-JANNSEN-16 route to this Part II; Temkin's Theorems 4.2.1 and 4.3.1 generalize it from P = {ℓ}′ to any P ⊇ char.

items.name: char(X), P-alterations and maximally dominating morphisms
items.statement: char(X) is the set of primes p = char k(x), x ∈ X. For a set of primes P, a P-alteration is an alteration whose degree is a P-number. For noetherian S with generic points η_i, η_S = ⊔ η_i; X → S is maximally dominating if it maps η_X to η_S, equivalently X ×_S η_S is dense in X; an alteration is a proper, surjective, maximally dominating, generically finite morphism.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Resolution of qe threefolds and surfaces
items.statement: Every quasi-excellent scheme of dimension ≤ 3 admits a desingularization ([CP14], unpublished at the time); published cases: qe surfaces ([Lip78]) and varieties of dimension ≤ 3 over fields of finite imperfection rank ([CP09]).
items.note: Cited input for Theorem 1.2.5. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7 plans resolution only in characteristic 0. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.5 (char(X)-altered desingularization)
items.statement: Let X be a scheme with a nowhere dense closed subset Z, admitting a finite-type morphism to a qe scheme S with dim S ≤ 3. Then there is a projective char(X)-alteration b : X′ → X with X′ regular and b⁻¹(Z) an snc divisor; if S = Spec k with k perfect, b can be chosen separable.
items.note: Proof: shrink S so that char(S) = char(X) (char(S) ∖ char(X) is finite for dominant f), then Cossart–Piltant and Theorem 4.3.1(i),(iii). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. Projectivity of b comes from Theorem 4.3.1(ii): universal P-resolvability (§4.1.4), which §4.3.2 cites through 4.3.1(i), does not include projectivity, so the blueprint should derive the first claim from (ii) (noted by REV-PAPER-TEMKIN-17).

items.name: Theorem 1.2.9 (char(S)-altered desingularization of morphisms)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be maximally dominating of finite type, Z ⊂ X nowhere dense closed, X separated and S of finite type over a noetherian qe threefold. (i) There are char(S)-alterations a : S′ → S, b : X′ → X with regular sources, projective, a quasi-projective f′ : X′ → S′ compatible with f and snc divisors W′ ⊂ S′, Z′ ⊂ X′ with Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′) and (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth. (ii) If S = Spec k with k perfect, moreover a is an isomorphism and b is separable.
items.note: From Theorem 4.3.1(ii),(iii). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Riemann–Zariski spaces of pointed schemes
items.statement: A pointed scheme is ε : Spec K → X with X quasi-compact and quasi-separated; a modification is a morphism with j an isomorphism and f proper. RZ_K(X) := lim X_i over all modifications, as a locally ringed space, with |RZ_K(X)| = lim |X_i| and O = colim π_i⁻¹O_{X_i}; constructible subsets are preimages of constructible subsets of some X_i. Tight modifications (ε schematically dominant) are cofinal.
items.note: Temkin's construction [Tem10, §3.2], here for non-dominant points too. Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 1 plans the valuation spectrum Spv and constructible-topology compactness, which this uses. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.3
items.statement: For X = RZ_K(X): (i) X is compact in the constructible topology and quasi-compact in the Zariski topology; (ii) each stalk O_{X,x} is a valuation ring and x ↦ O_{X,x} is a bijection RZ_K(X) → Val_K(X), the set of morphisms Spec O → X from valuation rings O of K extending the point.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.1.2, Lemma 3.1.3 and proof, p. 113
items.note: [Tem10, Cors. 3.2.4–3.2.5]. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.6 (functoriality and openness)
items.statement: A morphism of pointed schemes (η_L → Y) → (η_K → X) induces ψ : Val_L(Y) → Val_K(X) by restriction, compatible with RZ_L(Y) → RZ_K(X); if Y → X is of finite type, ψ is open and continuous in the Zariski and constructible topologies.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.1.5, Lemma 3.1.6 and proof, pp. 113–115
items.note: Reduce to K = k(X_i) and f flat of finite presentation by flattening; flatness lifts valuations. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Absolute Riemann–Zariski spaces
items.statement: Val_K = Val_K(Spec Z) is the set of all valuation rings of K; Val_K(X)′ ⊆ Val_K, the valuations with a centre on X, is compact in the constructible topology; for any L/K, ψ_{L/K} : Val_L → Val_K is continuous and open.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Tame, wild and unramified loci; S-, X- and P-tameness
items.statement: For algebraic L/K: L/K is x-tame for x ∈ Val_L if tame for x and ψ_{L/K}(x); Val^t_{L/K} is the tame locus, Val^w_{L/K} its complement; L/K is absolutely tame if Val^t = Val_L, S-tame if S ⊆ Val^t, X-tame if Val_L(X)′-tame (invariant under modification). char(S) is the set of nonzero residue characteristics of S; L/K is P-tame if char(Val^w_{L/K}) ∩ P = ∅; analogously the unramified locus Val^u_{L/K}.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6
items.statement: Any P-closed field K is P-tame; every algebraic extension of it, even when not P-closed, is P-tame too.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6, p. 116
items.note: From the tameness theorem 2.6.6. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.8
items.statement: (i) For L/l/k: Val^t_{L/k} = Val^t_{L/l} ∩ ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^t_{l/k}), and likewise for Val^u. (ii) If L = Kl for subextensions l/k and K/k, then ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^t_{l/k}) ⊆ Val^t_{L/K} and ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^u_{l/k}) ⊆ Val^u_{L/K}.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.10 (openness of the loci)
items.statement: For a finite extension L/K, the tame locus and the unramified locus are open in Val_L.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.9, Lemma 3.2.10 and proof, p. 117
items.note: Unramified: Chevalley's standard étale form is an open condition. Tame: pass to unramified extensions where L′ = K′(x_i^{1/n_i}). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.12 (tame distillation for fields)
items.statement: Let L/K be finite, S ⊆ Val_L compact in the constructible topology, and P = char(S ∩ Val^w_{L/K}) its wild primes set. Then there are a finite L′/L and a tower L′/K′/K with K′/K a P-extension and L′/K′ S′-tame, S′ = ψ_{L′/L}⁻¹(S). For any maximal P-extension K̄/K one can take K′ ⊆ K̄ and L′ = LK′.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.11, Theorem 3.2.12 and proof, pp. 117–118
items.note: LK̄/K̄ is S̄-tame since K̄ is P-closed; tameness is achieved over finite K_x locally, and quasi-compactness of S̄ with Lemma 3.2.10 makes finitely many suffice. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Galois alterations, tame actions and tame Galois coverings
items.statement: An alteration f : Y → X is Galois if Y/G → X is generically radicial for G = Aut_X(Y) (k(Y)/k(X) = purely inseparable then Galois with Aut_X(Y) the full Galois group), separable if generically étale. A finite group action is tame if every inertia group G_x (elements fixing x and acting trivially on k(x)) has order invertible in k(x). A Galois covering is a finite separable Galois alteration, tame if Aut_X(Y) acts tamely; Nor_K(X) is the normalization of X in K.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.4
items.statement: If X is noetherian, universally Japanese and integral and L/k(X) is an X-tame Galois extension, there is a modification X′ → X such that Nor_L(X′) → X′ is a tame Galois covering.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.3, Lemma 3.3.4 and proof, p. 119
items.note: The non-tame loci T_i = ∪_{(H,p), p | |H|} Y_i^H ∩ Y_i(p) are closed; a point of RZ_L(Y) in all of them would contradict y-tameness. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.7 (Galois closure preserves tameness)
items.statement: For L/K finite separable with Galois closure L′/K, T ⊆ Val_K, S = ψ_{L/K}⁻¹(T) and S′ = ψ_{L′/K}⁻¹(T): L/K is S-tame iff L′/K is S′-tame.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3, Lemma 3.3.7 and proof, p. 120
items.note: The proof as printed has its directions swapped and primes dropped (sourceIssues E2). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.6 (tame distillation of alterations)
items.statement: Let X be noetherian, universally Japanese and integral, Y → X an alteration, and P = P^w_{Y/X}, the wild primes set of Val_{k(Y)}(X)′ over k(X) (a subset of char(X) bounded by deg f). Then there is an alteration Y′ → Y such that Y′ → X factors as a tame Galois covering Y′ → X′ followed by a P-alteration X′ → X.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.5, Theorem 3.3.6 and proof, p. 120
items.note: Flatten so that Y = Nor_L(X); apply Theorem 3.2.12; pass to the Galois closure (Lemma 3.3.7); apply Lemma 3.3.4 over Nor_{K′}(X). Lemma 3.3.7 needs L′/K′ separable, which follows because X-tameness includes the trivial valuation. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Universal P-resolvability and pseudo-projective morphisms
items.statement: A noetherian X is universally P-resolvable if for every alteration Y → X and nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ Y there is a P-alteration f : Y′ → Y with Y′ regular and f⁻¹(Z) snc (universally separably P-resolvable if f can be chosen separable). A finite-type morphism is pseudo-projective if it is a local isomorphism followed by a projective morphism ([IT14b, 3.1.6]); for separated morphisms this is quasi-projectivity.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Gabber's modification theorem and monoidal desingularization
items.statement: If a finite group G acts tamely on a log regular (X, T) over a log regular (S, W) with trivial action on (S, W) and inertia specializing, there is a modification (X′, T′) of (X, T)/G with (X′, T′) → (S, W) log smooth ([IT14b, Th. 3.1.5; Th. 1.1]); the monoidal desingularization functor F^log ([IT14a, 3.4.9]) makes the source regular with snc boundary.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §1.3.5, p. 102; proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Step 10, p. 123
items.note: Cited inputs; the PrimeToDegreeAlterations briefs already name Gabber's log-modification proof as supplier work.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 (resolution of relative curves)
items.statement: Let S be noetherian qe with generic points η, f : X → S maximally dominating of finite type, Z ⊂ X nowhere dense closed. Assume S is universally (separably) P-resolvable for a set of primes P with char(X) ⊆ P, X_η is a smooth curve over η and Z_η étale over η. Then there are a projective (separable) P-alteration a : S′ → S, a projective modification b : X′ → (X ×_S S′)^pr and divisors W′ ⊂ S′, Z′ ⊂ X′ with S′, X′ regular, W′, Z′ snc, f′ : X′ → S′ pseudo-projective, (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth and Z′ = c⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4.2, Theorem 4.2.1 and proof, pp. 121–123
items.note: The [IT14b, Th. 3.4] proof with Step 4 replaced by tame distillation (Theorem 3.3.6). Under the printed hypothesis char(X) ⊆ P, that step needs the repair recorded in sourceIssues E1. The theorem is used only with char(S) ⊆ P. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(i)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a maximally dominating finite-type morphism of noetherian qe schemes, and S universally P-resolvable with char(S) ⊆ P. Then X is universally P-resolvable.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4.3, Theorem 4.3.1(i) and proof, p. 123
items.note: Copies the proof of [IT14b, Th. 3.5] with ℓ′ replaced by P and Theorem 4.2.1 in Step 6 (Step 4 uses an infinite P-extension of a finite field, possible since char(k) ∈ P). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(ii)
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses and a nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ X, there are projective P-alterations a : S′ → S and b : X′ → X with regular sources, a pseudo-projective f′ : X′ → S′ compatible with f and snc divisors W′, Z′ with Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′) and (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(iii)
items.statement: If S = Spec k with k perfect, one can moreover take a an isomorphism and b separable; in particular X is universally separably P-resolvable.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Remark 4.3.4 (refinement of Theorem 1.2.9)
items.statement: In Theorem 1.2.9 one can require X′ to be a char(X)-alteration of a subscheme of X ×_S S′ (rather than a char(S)-alteration), by resolving over an open S₀ with char(S₀) = char(X) and then embedding into a char(S)-alteration of S (outline).
items.note: An outline in the paper. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

routes.title: Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes, Part II: prime-to-degree alterations
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and PAPER-JANNSEN-16 under the same id; their briefs remain binding. They ask for Gabber's ℓ′-alterations; Temkin's paper generalizes them to P-alterations for any set of primes P containing the residue characteristics, and supplies the new ingredient, tame distillation. Add: char(X), P-alterations and maximal domination; Riemann–Zariski spaces of pointed schemes and Val_K(X) (Lemmas 3.1.3, 3.1.6), absolute RZ spaces; tame, wild and unramified loci and P-tameness (Lemmas 3.2.5, 3.2.8, 3.2.10); tame distillation for fields (Theorem 3.2.12); Galois alterations, tame actions and tame Galois coverings (Lemmas 3.3.4, 3.3.7) and tame distillation of alterations (Theorem 3.3.6); universal P-resolvability; de Jong's Galois and semistable variants and Gabber's ℓ′ theorems as the P = {ℓ}′ case; Gabber's modification theorem and monoidal desingularization; Theorem 4.2.1 on relative curves (with the repair of sourceIssues E1), Theorem 4.3.1(i)–(iii), Theorems 1.2.5 and 1.2.9 with Cossart–Piltant's threefold resolution as the base, and Remark 4.3.4. Import the tameness theorem and valued-field ramification from Local fields and ramification, Part II: ramification theory of general valued fields; de Jong's Theorem 4.1, flattening, normalization and semistable curve reduction from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5; log structures, Kato's chart criterion and log regularity from CrystallineCohomology CR.5:log-algebra; the valuation spectrum and constructible topology from Tau Ceti Foundations of adic spaces, Layer 1. Acceptance: P = {ℓ}′ recovers the ℓ′-theorems; in characteristic 0 (char(X) = ∅) a P-alteration is a modification; and a Galois alteration with wild inertia is not tame, so distillation genuinely enlarges it.
routes.reason: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 plans de Jong's alterations without degree control; PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and PAPER-JANNSEN-16 proposed this Part II for Gabber's degree-controlled strengthening, and DESIGN-AdicCoefficientsAndComparisonsPartII is pending. Temkin's char(X)-alterations are the general form of that theorem, so the paper coalesces with it, keeping its id, title, parent and area.

routes.title: Local fields and ramification, Part II: ramification theory of general valued fields
routes.brief: Extend Tau Ceti's Local fields and ramification roadmap from discretely valued local fields to arbitrary Krull valuations. The final theorem is Temkin's tameness theorem: a valued field of residual characteristic exponent p with no nontrivial p-extension is tame (Ann. Math. 186 (2017), Theorem 2.6.6). Plan: P-extensions and P-closed fields, split towers and separable distillation; henselian valued fields and henselization, Lemma 2.3.2 (l ⊗ k^h = ∏ l_i^h), Prüfer subalgebras (Lemma 2.3.4); the basic ramification tower k^s/k^t/k^u/k^h/k with unramified, strictly unramified, tame, henselian, totally ramified and purely wild extensions (Lemmas 2.3.8, 2.3.11, 2.4.2, 2.4.4), tame and separably tame fields, the tame closure and wild inertia with its Kummer description; the equivalent reformulations of §2.4.6; Pank's theorem for henselian fields (Kuhlmann–Pank–Roquette, or Ershov), Krasner's lemma for henselian valued fields, decompletion in height one (Lemma 2.5.2), Theorem 2.5.5 and Corollary 2.5.6; composed valuations and the finite-height chain (Lemma 2.6.3, Corollary 2.6.4), Abhyankar's finite-height bound, and Theorem 2.6.6. Import local-field ramification (Layers 2–3) as the rank-one discrete special case, Mathlib's Valuation, ValuationRing, HenselianLocalRing and IsKrasner, and Galois and profinite group theory. Acceptance: for discrete valuations the tame and purely wild notions agree with Layer 3's; an Artin–Schreier extension of F_p((t)) is purely wild; and a p-closed field of height two is tame via Corollary 2.6.4.
routes.reason: The atlas treats ramification only for local fields (Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification) and valuations only as points of adic spectra (AdicSpaces Layer 1). Henselization, tame and purely wild extensions of Krull-valued fields, Pank's theorem and tame fields have no owner. The theory is reusable beyond alterations: model theory of valued fields, and defect. So it is a Part II of the Tau Ceti local-fields roadmap, which DESIGN-LocalFieldsRamificationPartII will fold with the other Part IIs of that parent.

CR.5:log-algebra plans log structures, charts, fs monoids, and Kummer and log-smooth morphisms (Kato). Two general notions the paper uses belong beside them: the log structure O_X ∩ i_*O_U^× of a divisor (fs when the divisor is snc in a regular scheme), and Kato's log regular log schemes.

sourceIssues.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), Theorem 4.2.1 and Step 4 of its proof, pp. 121–122; page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: The source assumes universal P-resolvability of S for primes P satisfying char(X) ⊆ P. In Step 4 it invokes Theorem 3.3.6 to enlarge a so that its factorization consists of S̄ → S′, a tame Galois covering, followed by a : S′ → S, a P-alteration.
sourceIssues.correction: Either assume char(S) ⊆ P, which is how Theorem 4.3.1 uses the theorem, or keep char(X) ⊆ P and run Step 4 over S₀ := S minus the fibres over char(S) ∖ char(X) (finitely many, as in §4.3.2), which contains f(X) and has char(S₀) = char(X). Apply Theorem 3.3.6 to S̄ ×_S S₀ → S₀, obtaining a P-alteration and a Galois covering that is tame over S₀. Extend to S by normalization and closure of the modification, and resolve with the P-resolvability of S. Tameness is needed only over f(X), since X̄ lies over S₀ and Step 10 uses tameness of the action on X̄.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 3.3.6 yields a P^w_{S̄/S}-alteration, where P^w_{S̄/S} is the wild primes set of S̄ → S, a subset of char(S). With only char(X) ⊆ P it may contain primes outside P, at which S̄ → S can be wildly ramified although X is empty there. Then 'a P-alteration' does not follow as written. The paper's main results apply the theorem only through Theorem 4.3.1, where char(S) ⊆ P.
searched: 2026-09-29: the Annals article is freely available at annals.math.princeton.edu (SHA-256 1f4ac06f…) and was read; arXiv:1508.06255v2 (21 Feb 2017, 'final version') was compared: same statements and numbering, and E1–E3 are present in both.
2026-09-29: the Annals page and Crossref list no erratum. Not an exhaustive novelty claim.

review.reason: Confirmed on the page images of pp. 121–122. Theorem 4.2.1 assumes only char(X) ⊆ P, and Step 4 applies Theorem 3.3.6 to S̄ → S, which yields a P^w_{S̄/S}-alteration with P^w_{S̄/S} ⊆ char(S), not ⊆ P. In the ℓ′ case of [IT14b, Th. 3.4] the Sylow trick needed tameness only over X, so char(X) ⊆ {ℓ}′ sufficed there; distillation of the whole of S̄ → S does not have that locality. The theorem is applied only in Theorem 4.3.1, where char(S) ⊆ P, so no main result is affected; 'the proof' is the right scope. The proposed repair over S₀ (removing the finitely many fibres over char(S) ∖ char(X), as in §4.3.2) is plausible, but it is a sketch and the blueprint should prove it or restate the theorem with char(S) ⊆ P.

sourceIssues.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 3.3.7, p. 120; page image checked
sourceIssues.printed: The source calls the direct implication immediate and proves the inverse. It places the induced valuations on L_i in S′ for every K-isomorphism L_i = L, concludes that each L_i/K is tame, and identifies L with the composite of L₁, …, L_n to deduce tameness of L/K.
sourceIssues.correction: The inverse implication is obvious, so let us prove the direct one. … hence the induced valuations on L_i lie in S … and since L′ is the composite of L₁, …, L_n, the extension L′/K is tame too.
sourceIssues.reason: 'L′/K is S′-tame ⇒ L/K is S-tame' is the obvious direction, since subextensions of tame extensions are tame. The argument shows 'L/K S-tame ⇒ L′/K S′-tame', and the composite of the conjugates L_i is the Galois closure L′, not L. The same text is in arXiv v2.
searched: 2026-09-29: the Annals article is freely available at annals.math.princeton.edu (SHA-256 1f4ac06f…) and was read; arXiv:1508.06255v2 (21 Feb 2017, 'final version') was compared: same statements and numbering, and E1–E3 are present in both.
2026-09-29: the Annals page and Crossref list no erratum. Not an exhaustive novelty claim.

review.reason: Confirmed on the page image of p. 120: 'The direct implication is obvious, so let us prove the inverse one', followed by an argument that proves L/K S-tame ⇒ L′/K S′-tame, and ends with 'since L is the composite of L₁, …, L_n, the extension L/K is tame', where the composite of the conjugates is L′. The printed 'lie in S′' for valuations on L_i should also be S. Same text in arXiv v2, p. 20.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.6.3(ii), last paragraph, p. 112 (published version; page image checked); same in arXiv:1508.06255v2, p. 13
sourceIssues.printed: The source ends the argument if p|eLi/Ki; otherwise it asserts p|fLi/Ki. It then says p = char(K̃i) divides [L̃i : K̃i] and uses K̃i = (K̃i)u to conclude that L̃i/K̃i is not tame.
sourceIssues.correction: 'p, the residual characteristic exponent of the valued field K̃_i (that is, exp.char of the residue field of K), divides [L̃_i : K̃_i]'. The field K̃_i itself has characteristic p_i, which is 1 when i < n.
sourceIssues.reason: In §2.6.2, p_i = exp.char(k̃_i) equals 1 for i < n and p for i ≥ n. When p_i = 1 the reduction to this case is reachable: L_i/K_i is then automatically tame and defectless, so [L : K] = e_{L_i/K_i}·f_{L_i/K_i}, and p can divide f with p ∤ e. For example, take K̃_i strictly henselian of mixed characteristic (0, p) and L̃_i a degree-p extension of it. Then char(K̃_i) = 0 ≠ p. The argument survives with the corrected reading: K̃_i = (K̃_i)^u has separably closed residue field of characteristic p, so an extension of degree divisible by p cannot be tame.
